dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The bay empty-argument case (stderr, exit 2) was observed losing the whole command file in a live Claude Code 2.1.267 session (openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-10-new-bay-and-fleet/tasks.md §7.2), and `node src/cli.js next` on this trunk with two dockets printed SELECT A DOCKET and exited 2 — but the session-side loss for that stdout-only exit-2 case is still inferred; open question repro-next-trunk-040 closes it.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Each goal is an observable pass/fail statement about the four cli.js `!` lines, their Task sections, the untouched CLI exit contract, and a live session rendering the Task.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Every behaviour check was run against today's tree (exit 1) and a scratch prototype of the chosen wrapper (exit 0); after the success-criteria critic, a success-path check guards against an unconditional marker, and the only check passing today is the declared guard.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: The operator chose "4 ! lines + Task line" over next-only and lines-only; every excluded item carries its reason, and the stale stdout-only rationale the hidden-dependency critic found is now an explicit MVP item.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: Absorbing the exit code in the command file leaves the CLI exit contract (openspec/specs/command-surface/spec.md, README.md:132) intact for terminal and script callers, so no requirement conflicts with the fix.

problem: Every Waybill slash command that shells out to the CLI does so through a `!` line whose `if … fi` compound exits with node's status. When that status is non-zero, Claude Code reports `Shell command failed for pattern …` and never renders the command file — the `## Task` section, and every instruction in it, is lost (observed 2026-09-09, Claude Code 2.1.267, openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-10-new-bay-and-fleet/tasks.md §7.2).

The worst hit is `/waybill:next` on the trunk: both of its trunk outcomes exit 2 by contract — "no dockets open" (src/cli.js:208) and the `SELECT A DOCKET:` menu (src/cli.js:215-216) — so the Task branch written for that menu (commands/next.md:45) can never run in a session. `/waybill:bay` loses its Task on every error (empty argument, invalid ref, bay exists, …), and all four commands lose it outside a git repository or on a malformed booking. The operator gets a harness error instead of the menu or explanation the Task was written to deliver; 0.4.0 shipped with this, recorded as out of scope in openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-10-new-bay-and-fleet/design.md:75-81.
goals: Each of the four cli.js `!` lines (next, bay, new, status) exits 0 for every CLI outcome, carrying the CLI's stdout and stderr in its output plus a trailing `waybill: exited N` only when the CLI exited non-zero.

Each of those four `## Task` sections states what a trailing `waybill: exited N` means — no waybill was issued: show the block verbatim and do not run or improvise a leg — with next's existing `SELECT A DOCKET:` branch taking precedence.
The CLI exit contract (`next` exits 0 if and only if it issued exactly one waybill) is unchanged: no code change under src/ (comments only) and no diff to tests/cli.test.js.
In a live session, `/waybill:next` on a trunk with two dockets loads its Task and offers the docket choice instead of a shell-failure error.

successCriteria.criterion: `next` on a trunk with no dockets: the real `!` snippet exits 0 and shows the CLI message plus `waybill: exited 2` (today it exits 2)

check.cmd: R=$PWD; D=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$D"' EXIT; snip() { grep -m1 "^!\`" "$R/commands/$1.md" | sed -e "s/^!\`//" -e "s/\`\$//" -e "s|\${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}|$R|g" -e "s/\$ARGUMENTS//g"; }; repo() { d=$D/r; git init -q -b main "$d"; git -C "$d" -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -q --allow-empty -m init; echo "$d"; }; d=$(repo); s=$(snip next); out=$(cd "$d" && bash -c "$s"); test $? -eq 0 && echo "$out" | grep -q "no dockets open" && echo "$out" | grep -q "waybill: exited 2"

check.cmd: R=$PWD; D=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$D"' EXIT; snip() { grep -m1 "^!\`" "$R/commands/$1.md" | sed -e "s/^!\`//" -e "s/\`\$//" -e "s|\${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}|$R|g" -e "s/\$ARGUMENTS//g"; }; repo() { d=$D/r; git init -q -b main "$d"; git -C "$d" -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -q --allow-empty -m init; echo "$d"; }; d=$(repo); s=$(snip status); out=$(cd "$d" && bash -c "$s"); test $? -eq 0 && test -n "$out" && ! echo "$out" | grep -q "waybill: exited"

successCriteria.criterion: Each of next, bay, new and status carries the wrapper on its `!` line and a `waybill: exited` rule inside its `## Task` section

check.judgment: The operator starts `claude --plugin-dir <this bay>` (with the installed waybill@tinetti disabled so the bay's commands are the ones resolved) on a trunk with two dockets, runs `/waybill:next` (Task loads; the model offers the SELECT A DOCKET choice) and `/waybill:bay` with no argument (Task loads; the model relays the usage error and stops) — neither shows `Shell command failed for pattern`.

mvp.item: Append `2>&1 || echo "waybill: exited $?"` to the node call in the `!` line of commands/next.md, bay.md, new.md and status.md
mvp.reason: The single edit that stops every non-zero CLI outcome from discarding the command file, and folds stderr in so bay's errors reach the session whatever the unmeasured exit-0 stderr behaviour is.

mvp.item: One rule in each of those four `## Task` sections for a trailing `waybill: exited N`
mvp.reason: Once the Task loads for an error it needs an instruction for it; next's SELECT A DOCKET branch keeps precedence.

mvp.item: tests/bang-lines.test.js — extracts each real `!` line, substitutes the plugin root, runs it in fixture repos built with tests/helpers/repo-fixture.js, asserts exit 0 and the expected output on failure and success paths; imported from tests/index.js
mvp.reason: The failing-first test; nothing today executes a `!` line (closest patterns: tests/commands.test.js:152-181 extraction, :366-375 spawnSync).

mvp.item: Reword the "captures stdout only" rationale where it appears — README.md:143-144, openspec/specs/command-surface/spec.md:49-50 (the because-clause only; the SHALL stands), and the comments at src/cli.js:115-118 and :283
mvp.reason: After `2>&1` the `!` line carries stderr too, so the stated reason would be false; stdout stays the right stream because terminal and `--json` callers read it. Comment-only in src/, which the guard permits.

decisions.decision: Absorb the exit code in the command-file `!` line
decisions.rejected: Make `next` exit 0 on its trunk cases
decisions.reason: Reopens the spec'd contract (openspec/specs/command-surface/spec.md, README.md:132) that callers test against, and leaves bay's errors and not-a-repository still dropping the Task.

decisions.decision: Absorb the exit code in the command-file `!` line
decisions.rejected: A CLI `--session` flag that clamps exit to 0 and routes stderr to stdout
decisions.reason: New CLI surface, parsing and per-subcommand tests for what one shell operator already does.
`true` is not on the commands' restrictive allowed-tools list while `echo` is, and echo also tells the session which code the CLI exited with.

decisions.decision: Wrap all four cli.js `!` lines and add a Task rule to each
decisions.reason: bay loses its Task on every error and all four lose it outside a repository; the same one-line fix covers them.

decisions.decision: Acceptance needs both the scripted snippet test and a live-session check
decisions.reason: The script proves exit 0; only a live session proves Claude Code then renders the Task.

decisions.decision: Add a success-path check that the marker is absent on exit 0
decisions.reason: Success-criteria critic: an unconditional `; echo "waybill: exited $?"` passed every failure check while printing `exited 0` after every real waybill, which the new Task rule would read as no waybill.

decisions.decision: Gate completion on `npm test` plus a non-empty bang-lines suite
decisions.rejected: A TAP ok-line count above the 441 baseline
decisions.reason: Success-criteria critic: a dated count passes on any one added ok line and proves nothing the suite run does not.

decisions.decision: Reword the stdout-only rationale in README, living spec and src comments; guard allows comment-only src diffs

decisions.reason: Hidden-dependency critic: new-bay-and-fleet is archived and the rationale now lives in openspec/specs/command-surface/spec.md:49-50; a false stated reason is worse than a comment-only diff.
